premise.claim: Upstream gomonkey release notes for v2.14.x claim v2.13.0 crashes when CPU profiling or stack unwinding samples a patched function entry on amd64 ('invalid runtime symbol table') and clobbers R10 (11th ARM64 argument slot) / SIGBUSes on darwin/arm64.
premise.reportedComponent: github.com/agiledragon/gomonkey/v2 (test-only dependency of fluid, used by 88 test files: ApplyFunc 162x, ApplyPrivateMethod 86x, ApplyMethodFunc 71x, ApplyMethod 32x, ApplyMethodSeq 2x, NewPatches 2x)
premise.patchedComponent: go.mod/go.sum + vendored github.com/agiledragon/gomonkey/v2 v2.13.0 -> v2.14.4; no fluid source changes
premise.evidence: On linux/amd64 (go1.27.0 and go1.25.12), 1s of 100Hz CPU profiling over a 2.13.0-patched function completes cleanly with a parseable profile (results/unit-harness-base.log, TestCPUProfileOverPatchedEntry) — no 'invalid runtime symbol table'. Not positive evidence of absence (Go-version/unwind dependent), so not a blocker; the arm64 claims were not runnable on this x86 host. The important direction for THIS PR is the reverse: no 2.13.0->2.14.4 regression anywhere (see findings).
